john.cust: Hey team — streaming from our private deployment intermittently stalls for ~20-40s then dumps a big chunk of output. Happens only from our prod VPC (egress allowlist to redwood). Repro steps:
- Open a websocket to wss://inference.private.redwood.example/v1/streams
- send prompt, get partial tokens, then nothing for ~30s, then ~400 tokens in one burst

maya.sre: Thanks — this sounds like buffering/idle-timeout in a middlebox. Can you sanity-check whether there is an L7 proxy (nginx/ALB) in your egress path or an appliance that inspects TLS? Also need a tcpdump of the stream (first 60s).

john.cust: We're using a corporate NGFW + an egress proxy (sits in our VPC, 10.0.4.12). No internal TLS termination AFAICT. Attaching quick curl handshake output I captured:
```
$ curl -v -N -H "Connection: Upgrade" -H "Upgrade: websocket" "https://inference.private.redwood.example/"
* Connected to inference.private.redwood.example (52.44.11.99) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* ...
> GET /v1/streams HTTP/1.1
> Host: inference.private.redwood.example
> Upgrade: websocket
> Connection: Upgrade
< HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols
< Upgrade: websocket
< Connection: Upgrade
* Received 0 bytes in 30s, then 1.2KB in single TCP push
```

ben.platform: Two hypotheses: 1) TLS inspection appliance is buffering until it sees a record with FIN/PSH or a timeout, 2) SNI or cert mismatch causing renegotiation/rewrap and the appliance replays buffered data after reconnect. We saw similar with a transparent TLS proxy that doesn't forward 1-RTT application frames until it has full stream context.

maya.sre: To narrow it down, please run these diagnostics from a host that reproduces the issue and paste outputs:
1) `sudo tcpdump -w ws.pcap -s 0 -c 200 'host 52.44.11.99 and port 443'`
2) `openssl s_client -connect inference.private.redwood.example:443 -servername inference.private.redwood.example -alpn h2 -tls1_3`
3) capture NGINX (if present) config snippet around `proxy_buffering`, `proxy_http_version`, and `proxy_set_header Connection`.

john.cust: tcpdump attached (I truncated). Key bits — see repeated TLS handshake after stall:
```
... [TCP PSH] length=512 seq=1200
... ACK, then client hello
... full handshake resumes, then large TLS record with application data
```

maya.sre: That log is consistent with a middlebox triggering a TLS rehandshake/forwarding delay. Quick workarounds you can try while we dig in:
- Enable websocket application-level pings every 10s (reduces idle perceived by proxy).
- Configure TCP keepalive on client side (net.ipv4.tcp_keepalive_time=30).
- If you control the egress proxy, set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "Upgrade";` and increase proxy idle timeouts (proxy_read_timeout).

ben.platform: Also check SNI: if DNS resolves to an IP where an appliance presents a different cert, it may delay forwarding until it validates policy. `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername inference.private.redwood.example` + compare cert CN/SAN with expected.

john.cust: Tried enabling pings — reduces frequency but still see ~10s stalls on long streams. I don't manage the NGFW config; putting a support ticket with infra team now. Ticket: INF-2439.

maya.sre: We're opening an internal escalation with our infra side too. Could you share the exact time windows when you saw bursts? Our access logs show connection time + bytes; we'll cross-check. Also sending a small test build of the stream server that emits a 1-byte token every 5s to help identify where buffering begins.

oncall-bot: [incident created] INC-2026-0317-77 — streaming buffering suspected middlebox. Assigned: maya.sre, ben.platform. Priority: P2.

john.cust: Time windows: 2026-03-16 18:12:04 UTC, 18:35:21 UTC, 19:03:07 UTC. Attaching pcap excerpt and nginx conf snippet I can access. Thanks for the fast triage.

maya.sre: Good, we'll correlate. Next actions:
- you: share full pcap + whether egress uses a transparent TLS-inspection appliance
- us: deploy the test server and compare TCP/TLS timelines, check SNI and cert chain on our ingress
- if confirmed: recommend NGFW rule to exempt websocket traffic to redwood endpoints (allow raw TLS pass-through) or increase idle + disable buffering for that route.

ben.platform: FYI — if the customer cannot adjust the NGFW, we can provide a short-lived dedicated IP + cert pinning option for that customer so the middlebox cannot inspect (requires enterprise agreement). Discuss offline if needed.

john.cust: Copy — I'll follow up with infra and post updates here. Appreciate the help :thumbsup!
